full_judgment: 26. Further, the Enquiry Officer though recommended to absolve the petitioner from the charges framed against him, yet the punishing authority has inflicted a major punishment of compulsory retirement without giving any reason as to why they differed with findings and recommendations made by the Enquiry Officer. Mr. Md Nawab Ali the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner, has placed before us a decision of Mir Alauddin Ahmed vs Province of East Pakistan reported in 26 DLR 27 wherein it has been held that report of an officer holding inquiry is to be treated as a judicial order and reversal of such decision is permissible by the punishing authority provided the reasons are given. However, the punishing authority is not bound to accept the report given by the Enquiry Officer. As it appears from the aforesaid decision the punishing authority is under obligation to give reason if he differs with the finding of the Enquiry Officer. In the instant case although the punishing authority did not accept the finding and the recommendations of tile Enquiry Officer, but they did not give any reasons whatsoever as to why they differed with the findings and the recommendations made by the Enquiry Officer.
